payload.headline: SPY slips below its 1-month low; QQQ stays under its 200-day gate

summary.thesis: Tech (QQQ) is in a downtrend. The broad market (SPY) is sideways but closed just under its 1-month low and only slightly above its 200-day average. Fear is elevated, and only 18% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Stand aside, for both long-term and swing buyers.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 681.58 (its 200-day average, the market gate) would end the tech downtrend and support a selective stance. A SPY close below 729.79 would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.

payload.happening: SPY closed at 732.44, down 1.01% from 739.95. It is down 2.33% over 5 days and 4.76% over 20 days. That close is below its 1-month low of 733.00, set Nov 5. Per DATA, SPY is 0.1% below that level. QQQ closed at 656.95, down 0.73% from 661.75. It is down 2.64% over 5 days and 8.46% over 20 days, and sits 1.5% above its 1-month low of 647.05 (Nov 5). Both are well below their recent highs. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. The VIX fear gauge read 22.91 on Nov 16, up from 19.30. That puts it in the 'elevated' band (20–30), at the 88 mark of its 252-day range. The Nov 17 VIX reading isn't stored yet. No news since the last note is in DATA. NVDA reports earnings after today's close (estimated date). Per DATA, it carries big index weight, so its report moves the whole tech group.
payload.business: Read together, the three signals point the same way. Trend: QQQ is below both its 50-day (715.38) and 200-day (681.58) averages, so tech's trend is down. SPY is below its 50-day (762.89) but above its 200-day (729.79), so its long trend holds and its short trend is broken. Fear: a VIX of 22.91 is in the elevated band, meaning investors are paying more for protection than usual. Breadth: only 18% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so the selling is broad and not confined to a few big names. General knowledge, not from DATA: when weak trend, rising fear and narrow breadth line up, rallies tend to be harder to sustain until at least one of them turns. The broad market's last line of long-term trend support, SPY's 200-day average, is close to the current price.

worth.text: No valuation is implied. These are price-trend levels, not estimates of fair value.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: SPY is still 0.4% above its 200-day average of 729.79, so the broad market's long-term trend counts as up for now.
QQQ remains 1.5% above its 1-month low of 647.05, so tech's recent low is holding.
The VIX at 22.91 is elevated but below the 'high' band (30+) and under its 252-day max of 31.05.
bear: QQQ is in a downtrend, 3.7% below its 200-day average and 8.9% below its 50-day average. The market gate stays active.
SPY closed at 732.44, below its 1-month low of 733.00. Per the trend gates, a close below that level means the decline is continuing.
Breadth is down to 18% of stocks above their 50-day averages, and fear rose from 19.30 to 22.91, into the elevated band.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average. Per the market gate, a close above it ends the tech downtrend. That would support a selective stance.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5). SPY closed just below it. A close back above it would mean the recent low is holding.
SPY 200-day average. A close below it would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: QQQ remains below its 200-day gate of 681.58. SPY closed under its 1-month low, breadth is at 18%, and fear is elevated. All three readings argue against new buying. That stays true until QQQ closes back above 681.58 or SPY recovers 733.00 with its 200-day average of 729.79 intact.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 656.95, 8.9% below its 50-day average of 715.38. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: NVDA reports earnings after the close on Nov 17 (estimated date). Per DATA, its report moves the whole tech group. It lands with QQQ 1.5% above its 1-month low and 3.7% below its 200-day gate. GDP (second estimate, Q3) and October Personal Income and Outlays, which includes the PCE inflation measure, are both due Nov 25 at 08:30. The latest stored VIX is from Nov 16; the Nov 17 reading isn't stored yet.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 681.58 (its 200-day average) would end the tech downtrend per the market gate and support a selective stance. A close above 715.38 (its 50-day average) would pass the pipeline's market check.
A SPY close below 729.79 (its 200-day average) or a QQQ close below 647.05 (its 1-month low) would mean the decline is widening. That would reinforce standing aside.
payload.what_changed: The last note (Nov 16) had QQQ at 661.75 and SPY nearing its 1-month low. Since then, QQQ fell to 656.95 and SPY closed at 732.44, just below its 1-month low of 733.00. Breadth dropped from 25% to 18%. Fear moved from the normal band (19.30) into the elevated band (22.91, Nov 16 reading). The moving gates shifted slightly. QQQ's 200-day average is now 681.58 (was 681.41) and its 50-day is 715.38 (was 716.59). SPY's 50-day is 762.89 (was 763.52) and its 200-day is 729.79 (was 729.58). The stance is unchanged: stand aside. This is research, not advice.
